blocks.text: Aramaic buṭmā, from which arab. [=Arabic] buṭm is borrowed, Fraenkel [=Siegmund Fraenkel, Die aramäischen Fremdwörter im Arabischen] 139. The single occurrence of buṭnīm in the Targum is a learned conjecture. Talmudic buṭmā Rh. [=Rosh ha-Shanah] 23^{a}. Bb. [=Bava Batra] 80^{b}. jKil. [=Jerusalem Talmud, tractate Kilayim] 1, 27^{a}. Targ. [=Targum] Jes. [=Isaiah] 1, 30. 6, 13 (TW. [=Levy, Chaldäisches Wörterbuch über die Targumim] אלה). 1 S. [=1 Samuel] 17, 2. 2 S. [=2 Samuel] 18, 9. Hos. [=Hosea] 4, 13. Onkelos [=Targum Onkelos] and jGn. [=Jerusalem Targum on Genesis] 35, 4. The Samaritan has דחלתה (דהלאה), and thus misunderstood the word and thought of ʾelōᵃh.

bōṭem, which BJ. [=Ben Jehuda, Millōn] cites from Aßafs [=Asaf Judaeus, medical book] boṭmīm, is not Hebrew: it has been retained from the Syriac source. Ph. [=Eretz-Yisrael Hebrew] Hasade [=Hasade, Hebrew agricultural monthly] 6, 206.

The resin of the terebinth, buṭm, Musil [=Musil, Arabia Petraea III] 3, 230. Nuwairī [=an-Nuwairī, Nihāyat al-arab] (E. Wiedem. [=Wiedemann, Beiträge zur Geschichte der Naturwissenschaften] 49, 19). ^{1}) ʿilk el-buṭm, resin of the حبّة الخضراء [ḥabbat al-khaḍrāʾ], comes from the Maghreb, Eretz Yisrael, Syria and neighboring regions. As distinct from this, pistachio resin is called ^{2}) ʿilk el-anbāṭ,†) while mastic is called ^{3}) ʿilk al-rūmī. Kašef [=Kachef er-rumūz, transl. Leclerc] Sha [=Steinschneider, Heilmittelnamen der Araber] 1393 ff. [=and the following (pages)] has ^{1}) and ^{3}) likewise, but ^{2}) without translation, and ^{4}) ʿilk šaǵar ul-fustuḳ: pistachio-tree gum.
